text:
anya: Quick idea — do we want a micro-shard prefetch protocol that exposes per-layer offsets + eviction hints to the runtime? Thinking about reducing warmup latency for long LLMs.
jordan: Short answer: yes if it stays tiny. What's "micro-shard" vs a normal shard?
liam: Micro-shard = contiguous byte ranges inside a shard (often per-layer or per-block). We stream the earliest layers first so KV cache priming doesn't block.
sasha: Sounds useful. We need an interface boundary: loader should remain dumb about scheduling; runtime sends PrefetchHint requests and loader maps to transport reads. Keep manifest optional.
anya: Agreed. Proposal: keep sidecar metadata small (<128KB) that lists (shard_id, offset, length, logical_priority). If sidecar absent, fall back to classic manifest.
jordan: Can't we infer offsets from safetensors layer headers? In some checkpoints yes, but not always (packed tensors). Sidecar makes it explicit and uploader-friendly.
liam: Tradeoffs: more metadata to produce & sign on upload, slight uploader complexity. Benefit: much faster cold-start for typical chat flows where first N layers determine response latency.
sasha: Draft loader API idea: PrefetchHint(shard_id, offset, length, priority) + ReadCursor handle returned for streaming reads. Runtime keeps priorities and can batch hints.
anya: Rough proto sketch:```proto
message PrefetchHint {
  string shard_id = 1;
  uint64 offset = 2; // byte offset in shard
  uint64 length = 3; // bytes to stream
  uint32 priority = 4; // lower = higher priority
}

rpc Prefetch(PrefetchHint) returns (ReadHandle) {}
```
jordan: Important: batching and coalescing must live in runtime to avoid N small RPCs to storage. Runtime can group same-shard hints into one range read. Also need backpressure signals.
liam: Perf concern: object store small-read penalty. We should prefer compact ranges and let runtime coalesce nearby micro-shards. Also add a hint `expect_sequential` for reads used for streaming to enable read-ahead.
anya: Security: sidecars must be signed and checksumed like weights. Same provenance flow. If signature mismatch -> fall back to full shard fetch and log a warn.
ml-deploy-bot: Note: tagging this thread and creating tracking ticket infra/eng-ml#TODO.
sasha: Warmup modes proposal: `fast_start` (prime first N logical layers synchronously) vs `progressive_stream` (stream micro-shards prioritized by predicted attention horizon). Offer as runtime config per-route.
jordan: How to pick N for fast_start? Default heuristics: small models -> N=2 layers, decoder-only LLMs -> N based on kv priming depth (empirically 4-6). We should expose as tunable in route config.
liam: Follow-ups: uploader CL to emit sidecar, runtime change to accept PrefetchHint and coalesce, loader shim to map ReadHandle to filesystem/HTTP object reads, and end-to-end bench: cold-start 0->1 token latency for 70B and 13B.
anya: Sg. I'll open RFC with proto, sidecar schema, and perf plan. Will include micro-benchmark harness + fallback metrics. cc @jordan @liam @sasha
sasha: I'll prototype the runtime coalescer this week and test against s3 emulator. 👍
jordan: SGTM. If prototype shows >15% cold-start win with <2% uploader overhead, we should move forward.
liam: I'll draft the sidecar spec and signing steps.
anya: Thanks all — this feels like a small, high-leverage refactor to the warmup path.
